# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-8 (Extended v88)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Winter Year 2, late afternoon/evening)**: Funeral procession for Mother Crucifixion en route to Vaugirard cemetery; Valjean's escape plan executing; Cosette retrieved from fruit-seller. Key dates: 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, Valjean's theft and flight; Waterloo/Hougomont June 17-18); 1817 (young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral tenure); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest; Javert's revelation; TRIAL SEQUENCE in Arras; Valjean's self-revelation; acquittal of Champmathieu; RETURN TO M. SUR M. before six a.m.; Fantine's death; Valjean arrested beside death-bed; VALJEAN ESCAPES same evening)**; December 1823 (Montfermeil rescue of Cosette, 1,500-franc payment to Thénardier); **December 26, 1823 (Valjean and Cosette returned to Paris via Barrier Monceaux)**; 1824 spring onward (decrepit building lodging; winter passed; spring advanced); **Summer Year 2**: Achieved sanctuary inside walled garden compound, le Petit-Picpus district. **Winter Year 2 (Current)**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak; body placed in vault beneath grand altar during 11 p.m.–midnight procedures; **Following day (sun declining, afternoon/evening)**: Funeral procession departing toward Vaugirard cemetery on Boulevard du Maine; **procession reached cemetery at dusk**; sun touching dome, cemetery closing in five minutes; light going early as typical for season.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles); **English harbor towns** (Dunstead, Yarlby, Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Gulhaven): Luvie, Wilwick, Gadrek Prydenridge, Isric, Jotho, Tatho Brackick, Harine Lindmere, Pelde Stenson, Pelde Stenworth, Yera Stenworth, Yewyn Haskick, Orrald the Younger (died of festering wound at Torton), Davus (Stenworth variant), Davus Stenworth, Ismira Stenson (rumored dead of plague per Harine Lindmere via peddler), Davus and Pelde Stenson wed at Torton with half parish present, couple now living in Torton; recurring motifs include weather, commerce, harvests, lame horses, mud, chimneys, gulls over fish heads, baker's boy late, oven line growing long. Arras; Waterloo; Toulon; Paris districts including Mouffetard quarter. **Gorbeau House** (Rue de la Cosette area, Mouffetard): Decrepit lodging where Valjean and Cosette previously lodged; old woman portress; Javert's surveillance station. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; market-gardens, timber-yards, unpaved roads; roads all ruts and puddles after thaw. **Number 62 Rue Petit-Picpus (CONVENT CARRIAGE GATE)**: Ajar gate, courtyard, vine-hung walls, tall trees above wall. **Wall (approximately 18 feet)**: Extends from niche to house 49 Rue Polonceau; shorter fragment along Rue Droit-Mur. **CONVENT COMPLEX - THREE BUILDINGS**: (1) **Great Convent**: Inhabited by Bernardines-Benedictines nuns; gloomy building, heavily shuttered window with sheet zinc. (2) **Boarding-school**: Where scholars lodged. (3) **Little Convent**: Building with garden housing aged nuns of various orders destroyed in Revolution. **INTERIOR GARDEN (Great Convent)**: Vast oblong area; alley of large poplars; forest trees in corners; solitary gnarled tree, fruit-trees, vegetable beds, melon patch with glass frames, old well, stone benches, grass and green mould. **PARLOR (Great Convent)**: Monstrous lattice of iron bars (squares less than 1.5 inches diagonal) riveted by clenched-fist fastenings; behind lattice: barrier of black shutters reinforced with gingerbread-yellow wooden beams, always closed; behind shutters: nun's voice screened by iron grating and plate with thousand holes; slat opens revealing nun's mouth and chin only, covered with black veil, guimpe, shroud. **BURIAL LOCATIONS**: Lower hall of church communicates with street, no men enter except doctor of dead; **Vaugirard cemetery**: Ancient cemetery outside regulations, has special Permission from Prefecture for nuns to be taken there at nightfall; venerable enclosure planted like old-fashioned French garden with straight alleys, box, thuya-trees, holly, ancient tombs beneath aged cypress-trees, very tall grass; tragic and lugubrious in evening; cemetery closed at dusk; accessed via grand alley through cypress-trees, narrows to waste land and thicket. **Boulevard du Maine**: Route of funeral procession. **Rue Chemin-Vert**: Location of deaf fruit-seller (good old friend of Fauchelevent), who provided bed for Cosette overnight. **Grave-digger's dwelling (Vaugirard cemetery)**: Unfurnished garret; packing-case as commode; butter-pot as drinking-fountain; straw mattress as bed; thin woman and children piled on tattered carpet fragment; shows signs of desperate search (covers displaced, rags scattered, broken jug, evidence of beating, overturned interior).

## Convent of the Bernardines of the Perpetual Adoration
[Same as before—order lineage, dress, austerity, vows, operational rules, reparation practice, possessions rule, hourly bells, chanting, men allowed]

**MOTHER CRUCIFIXION'S DEATH AND FUNERAL COMPLETION**: Mother Crucifixion died at daybreak (Winter Year 2). Retained consciousness to last moment, spoke to community then to angels, gave final commands. Prioress described her death as "precious"—smiled, community felt she was regaining life in God. Sisters laid out body. **VAULT BURIAL EXECUTED** (11 p.m.–midnight, same night): Fauchelevent closed coffin; sisters carried coffin to chapel; office for dead said; community returned to cloister. Fauchelevent came with iron bar; Mother Precentors and Mother Ascension present; vault opened beneath grand altar, coffin lowered, vault closed again—no trace, government has no suspicion. Doctor signed death passport. **FUNERAL PROCESSION** (following day, afternoon/evening): Undertaker company brought empty coffin for appearance; hearse ornamented with skulls, cross-bones, tears; coffin covered with white cloth, large black cross; mourning-coach with priest in surplice and choir boy in red cap; two undertaker's men in gray uniforms trimmed with black walked beside hearse; Fauchelevent limped behind in laborer's garments; procession heading toward Vaugirard cemetery; soil light and wet with winter rains, clogged hearse wheels, retarded speed. **ARRIVAL AT CEMETERY**: Hearse skirted cypress-trees, quitted grand alley, turned into narrow alley, entered waste land, plunged into thicket, indicating proximity of burial place. Sun touching dome at arrival; cemetery closed in five minutes. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage. Light went early as seasonal.

## Prioress and Vocal Mothers (1819-1825 Period)
**Mademoiselle de Blemeur (Mother Innocente)** (Prioress, 1819-1825): Age ~sixty; short, thick; "singing like a cracked pot"; excellent woman; only merry one in convent; learned, erudite, wise; proficient in history; descended from Marguerite de Blemeur, author of _Lives of the Saints of the Order of Saint-Benoît_; re-elected. Upon entering on day of death arrangements, double form of preoccupation imprinted on countenance; rose and exclaimed with loquacity of dam breaking away, speaking extensively about Mother Crucifixion's death and spiritual merit. **Vocal Mothers**: Mother Sainte-Honorine; Mother Sainte-Gertrude (treasurer); Mother-Saint-Ange; Mother Annonciation (sacristan); Mother Saint-Augustin (nurse; only malicious one); Mother Sainte-Mechtilde (directs singing); Mother des Anges; Mother Saint-Joseph; Mother Sainte-Adélaide; Mother Miséricorde; Mother Compassion; Mother Providence; **Mother Présentation** (future prioress 1847); Mother Sainte-Céligne; Mother Sainte-Chantal; **Mother Crucifixion** (deceased, Winter Year 2); **Four Mother Precentors** (present at vault opening); **Mother Ascension** (present at vault opening).

## Jean Valjean's Crisis, Escape Execution, and Current Status
**PSYCHOLOGICAL STATE DURING CRISIS**: Upon learning nun died and funeral procedures commencing, confronted with immediate danger: body removal and convent doors opening; police swarming streets. Turned pale; thought of descending to "terrible street" made him shudder. Pictured entire police force engaged in swarming quarter, agents on watch, sentinels everywhere. **ESCAPE EXECUTION**: Valjean hid inside coffin before Fauchelevent nailed upper plank. Shortly after nailing, felt himself carried out and driven off. Knew from diminution in jolting when leaving pavements for earth road. Divined from dull noise crossing Bridge of Austerlitz. Understood at first halt they were entering cemetery; at second halt, recognized burial was imminent. Possessed gloomy talent—man who has been prisoner understands contracting to fit diameter of escape; can live long time in box, find air where none exists, economize breath for hours, stifle without dying. Demonstrated composure and coolness in crisis—powerful tranquility contagious to others. Never was there more critical situation, never more complete composure. All combinations thought out had been progressing favorably since preceding day. **COSETTE'S RETRIEVAL**: After cemetery procedures, Fauchelevent and Valjean (emerged from grave after burial) went to fetch Cosette from fruit-seller in Rue du Chemin-Vert, where she had been deposited previous day. Cosette passed twenty-four hours trembling silently, understanding nothing; trembled so she wept; neither eaten nor slept; fruit-seller plied hundred questions without obtaining reply except melancholy, unvarying gaze; Cosette betrayed nothing of what seen/heard in last two days; divined passing through crisis; deeply conscious need to "be good"; fear is mute; no one guards secret like child.

## Fauchelevent's Crucial Role and Current Status
**Identity**: Old crippled gardener admitted approximately two years previously (1821) on Valjean's (Mayor Madeleine's) recommendation after cart accident. Limps; takes nearly quarter hour to traverse short distances; complains of aching back as usual. **COSETTE PLAN EXECUTED**: Used service door opening on courtyard; knocked, porter opened; placed Cosette in vintage basket on back, covered—"Father Fauchelevent goes out with his basket—perfectly natural"; left her with deaf fruit-seller in Rue Chemin-Vert (good old friend) who provided little bed; told fruit-seller in shout that child was his niece, to keep her until following day. **VALJEAN PLAN EXECUTED**: Placed Valjean in coffin; transported coffin in hearse to Vaugirard cemetery with Valjean inside. **CEMETERY OPERATIONS**: At cemetery, after hearse halted, Fauchelevent confronted new situation—Father Mestienne is dead; replaced by "little Father Lenoir" (jug of red wine, Surêne Paris wine). Fauchelevent offered drink to new grave-digger "conscript" but avoided explaining payment (generally Mestienne paid; left payment question intentionally dark). New grave-digger claimed to have accepted Mestienne's reversion; works scrivener's stall in market Rue de Sèvres (Umbrella Market), writes love letters to raw soldiers mornings, digs graves evenings. **CRITICAL COMPLICATION**: Grave-digger had lost his card (cemetery entry authorization). Without card, could not return to cemetery. Fauchelevent revealed he found card on ground after grave-digger left, buried corpse, filled grave, did work himself; porter would return card; conscript wouldn't pay fifteen francs. **FAUCHELEVENT'S PEACE OF MIND**: Though troubled by souls' uncanny sensation in place, perfectly composed; knew grave-digger Gribier wouldn't arrive (conscript at home searching lodgings for card, which Fauchelevent carried); cemetery was closed; no apprehension of interference. Slackened his pace but could not detain hearse. **CHARACTER**: Grateful, talkative, excitable; calls Valjean "Father Madeleine"; speaks freely; peasant of Picardy. Perceived generous action as dying man perceives glass of good wine; old egoist finding sweetness in gratitude toward end of days. Air of convent destroyed personal selfishness; renders good action absolutely necessary; enlisted self-devotion, good will, old rustic cunning. **RELATIONSHIP WITH FATHER MESTIENNE**: Within last two years, made good Father Mestienne (grave-digger at Vaugirard cemetery, chubby-cheeked person), drunk at least ten times; played with him, made him dance according to whim; Mestienne's head adjusted to Fauchelevent's will. Fauchelevent's confidence had been perfect—though now grave-digger is replaced. **STATUS**: Valjean's only known ally and protector in Paris; sole person aware of Valjean and Cosette's presence; executed escape plan successfully; retrieved Cosette successfully.

## Javert's Pursuit and Ongoing Investigation
**REASSIGNMENT TO PARIS** (January 1823): When Valjean escaped M. sur M. jail, Javert attached to Paris police force. **NEWSPAPER REPORT** (December 1823): Newspaper announced Valjean's death; Javert remarked "That's a good entry." **REACTIVATION**: Police report concerning child abduction in Montfermeil revived Javert's memory; suspected Valjean had sought daughter. **JAVERT'S SECRET INVESTIGATION**: Without telling anyone, took coach to Montfermeil; followed mysterious lodger to Gorbeau house; hired room, listened at lodger's door; Valjean foiled spy by silence. **REASONS FOR SECRECY**: (1) Slightest indiscretion might alert Valjean; (2) Recapturing ex-convict reputed dead was magnificent success; (3) Javert had taste for unforeseen. **PURSUIT ESCALATION**: Old woman suspected lodger intending to leave, warned Javert; Javert waited behind trees with two men at night. **ESCAPE FROM MOUFFETARD**: Valjean cut street lantern rope; Javert found disorder in lantern, led astray. **STRATEGIC PURSUIT**: Followed from tree to tree; did not arrest hastily (considered it risky, preferred gloating anticipation). **CURRENT STATUS** (Winter Year 2): Even when saw Valjean escaped, sure convict could not be far off; established sentinels, organized traps and ambuscades. Free press embarrasses police; arbitrary arrests denounced by newspapers; police agents afraid of mistakes.

## Narrative Commentary
Author remarks that burial of Mother Crucifixion under altar of convent is perfectly venial offence—one of faults which resemble duty. Nuns committed it without difficulty, even with applause of own consciences. In cloister, "government" is only intermeddling with authority, always questionable. Rule takes precedence over code. Tribute to Cæsar never anything but remnants of tribute to God. Prince is nothing in presence of principle. Notes that souls of Fauchelevent and Valjean troubled even when recovered, something uncanny about them—sinister bewilderment inspired by place.
